name: Workflow Agent Node
description: On-demand Agent guide for delegating to and reading connected Agent nodes through backend and wf-bridge actions.

roleProfile.howToRead: Read your own profile with node Harness/scripts/wf-ui-control.mjs workflow-context --project . ; the context carries your roleProfile block with displayName, roleTitle, responsibility, capabilities, and roleProfileRef. roleProfileRef points at the markdown profile file under Harness/a2a/agent-roles/. Your roleTitle comes from the canonical vocabulary (ceo, manager, implementer, reviewer, verifier, planner, terminal-controller) or a free-form role. Act inside your responsibility; ask the coordinating agent before expanding scope.

decisionFlow: Understand the task from the user request.
Decide whether team collaboration is needed: simple requests are handled directly with no team; complex or multi-skill work gets a team.
Select the subagent mode per subagentModes: default to built-in-subagents; use wf-node-subagents only when the user explicitly asks for canvas Agent nodes.
Choose the required roles from the canonical roleTitle vocabulary: ceo, manager, implementer, reviewer, verifier, planner, terminal-controller.
Find existing agents by role, runtime, provider, capability, or title.
Exactly one unambiguous match: auto-connect that agent.
No match and the task target is clear: create an agent with a full role profile (displayName, roleTitle, responsibility, capabilities, roleProfileRef).
Multiple matches or an unclear target: ask the user; never blindly create or connect.
Share durable context through Markdown nodes, referenced by nodeId only.
Send structured requests with a requestId, wait via Timer wakeup messages, and aggregate replies per request.
Tick the connected Goal node's items as they finish; call goal.complete when every item is checked; report to the user in plain language.

goalPlanning.guidance: Plans, plan tables, and goal setting default to the workflow Goal node. Do not use runtime built-in goal/task tools for planning when a workflow map is present.
flow: Before planning, read workflow-context to find the Goal node connected to you (direct edge or same Timer/Agent group).
Goal node found and connected: write the plan with goal.add / goal.replace, tick progress with goal.check / goal.uncheck, and call goal.complete when every item is checked.

Goal node found but not connected: connect it with node Harness/scripts/wf-ui-control.mjs connect --actor <your-graph-node-id> --from <your-graph-node-id> --to <goal-node-id> --relation goal, then move it above your node with node Harness/scripts/wf-ui-control.mjs node-map --action moveNode --node <goal-node-id> --x <your-x> --y <your-y-above>.

No Goal node exists: create one with node Harness/scripts/wf-ui-control.mjs node-map --action createNode --type goal --title '<task> goal' --x <your-x> --y <your-y-above>, then connect it as above and write the plan into it.
Respect singleGoalPerGroup: one Goal per Timer/Agent group; if goal_already_bound is returned, use the existing Goal.

subagentModes.note: 2x2 subagent strategy matrix. Mode is set via Agent node settings or detected from natural language; unspecified defaults to built-in-subagents.

matrix.behavior: Use the current runtime's native subagent mechanism. Do NOT create WF canvas Agent nodes.
Create/connect WF Agent nodes on canvas. Use mailbox for communication. Timer/Markdown/Goal nodes visible and collaborative.

subagentModes.runtimeDegradation: If the current runtime has no native subagent adapter and mode is built-in-subagents, record clear degradation evidence and inform the user. Codex main can use wf-node-subagents to dispatch tasks to Claude Code implementer nodes and aggregate replies.

structuredRequests.guidance: Give every team request a requestId and reuse it for all messages of that request. Reference shared Markdown nodes in contextRefs by nodeId only — never inline Markdown bodies or long content in the message text.
structuredRequests.inputEnvelope: A structured request arrives in your terminal as a compact prefix before the text, e.g. [harness-request req-20260812-0001 to-role=implementer contextRefs=markdown-2a1] <text>. On receiving one, reply via send-agent-message with the SAME requestId and set --reply-to to the message id you are answering, so the sender can aggregate the replies.
rules: requestId: sender-generated; the receiver echoes it in replies so you can aggregate them.
replyTo: set to the message id you are answering.
contextRefs: nodeId references only; the receiver reads the node through typed actions.

wakeupMessages.guidance: Timers are the only source of wakeup messages; the Goal node never wakes agents. When a wakeup message arrives (type 'wakeup'), read it on your next turn. It carries timerNodeId, scheduledAt, firedAt, and goalNodeId when the group has a Goal node.
wakeupMessages.goalCheck: When the wakeup message references a Goal node, read the Goal state first and tick its items before continuing work.

goalTicking.guidance: Tick Goal plan items as you finish them with goal.check; use goal.uncheck when an item is back in progress. When every item is checked, call goal.complete. If goal.complete returns goal_items_pending, check the listed items first, then retry.

markdownBlackboard.guidance: Share durable context through Markdown nodes; reference them by nodeId only in requests. Before writing, find the node, acquire a lock, write with the current revision, then release the lock. On markdown_conflict, reread, merge, and retry with the fresh revision.

controlSurface.storage: Harness/a2a/nodes/** and terminal logs are runtime records, not manual control surfaces.

prohibitions: Never edit `Harness/a2a/**/state.json` directly — use typed actions.
Never edit node-home files, terminal logs, or session state files.
Never inline Markdown node bodies in a message payload; reference them by nodeId only.
